audit_items.proof_trace: `liquidate_calculate_seize_ctokens` returns `seize_ctokens.floor()` (L1073); when the repay amount is small relative to collateral price, this floors to 0. `liquidation_inner` has no guard asserting `seized_ctokens > 0` before L776. When `seized_ctokens = 0`, `obligation.withdraw_ctokens(0)` calls `split_ctoken(0)`, which immediately aborts via `assert!(amount > 0)` in ctoken_table.move:82. Because Move is atomic, the entire ADL transaction reverts, leaving bad debt unclearable for affected obligations.
audit_items.attack_scenario: An obligation with a tiny debt balance (e.g., 1 wei of a low-price debt token) and high-price collateral (e.g., BTC) can produce `seized_ctokens = 0` even when the obligation is unhealthy and ADL-eligible; every ADL transaction targeting it will abort, permanently blocking bad-debt clearance for that obligation. Alternatively, an obligation holding zero ctokens of the specified `CollateralType` (but non-zero other collateral) passes `ensure_liquidate_borrow_allowed` yet still aborts at `withdraw_ctokens(0)`, making that collateral-type ADL path permanently unusable.
